judges.verdict: Value, translucency, thickness and overall periwinkle colour are close to the Cycles reference at rest (mean luma within ~3 levels), so at a glance it reads as ice. Side by side, though, the ring bodies read as cloudy, marbled glass or acrylic: isotropic high-contrast white cloud blobs and blocky dark-blue patches, with rounded, melted, pillow-like silhouettes and end caps. The reference is frosted, chiselled carved ice with long darker bands along the ring, crisp TIR lines, cracks and fine scrape frost. Further CG tells: a featureless mint inner band in front of the orb in the eye pose, mint rims, dotted iso-line contours with pixel sparkle at 2.5–3.4x the reference's fine-scale energy, and a hold close-up that lacks the reference's dramatic internal refraction (dark far-wall line, white refracted orb strip, facet glints).
strengths: Mean value and colour at rest match closely. ref_F000 vs q00_rest in the same boxes: band left L 203.8 vs 201.8, band right 190.0 vs 192.6, upper rings 196.5 vs 199.7, lower arcs 187.0 vs 189.7. Eye pose outer ring L 165 vs 170 with matching spread (sd 31 vs 30). Not too milky, not too dark at rest; keep this exposure.

Thickness and volume read well: chunky, translucent rings with the sky, mountains and horizon visible through them, and the front band refracts the rings behind it (q00, q02). The ice-behind-ice pass works.
The orb glow transmits through the front band at rest as a soft bright area (q00 orb box L 247 vs 239), as in F000.
Frosted, whiter end blocks beyond the band's TIR bars at rest (q00 row y=385: L 227–241 vs F000 230–235), and the TIR bars exist at both band ends, in the right places.
Outlines are irregular rather than perfect tori. No visible piece seams at the ring joints at rest, no gradient banding, no blocky half-res thickness artefacts.
In the expand pose (p05) the open ring ends read as flat cut faces (top arc end at x≈820–880, y≈60–150).
Rim brightness is in the right range (about 220, F045 rim about 221). Only its hue and uniformity are off.

issues.title: Ring bodies read as cloudy marbled glass: isotropic high-contrast cloud blobs and blue patches instead of frosted ice with structure running along the ring
issues.evidence: crop_q01_loop15_hero.jpg and zoom_ice_material/q01_center_2x.png: the engine's big ring (q01_loop15.png x≈560–640, y≈200–500) is covered in soft white cloud-shaped blobs and saturated blue patches, like clouds seen through clear glass. loop_F015 shows the same ring as evenly frosted ice whose main structure is a darker band running along the inner edge. q00 band (zoom q00_band_2x.png): engine shows camouflage blotches; F000 shows a clean flat face with fine horizontal scrape frost. Measured, q00_rest vs ref_F000: band right (x790–860, y352–410) luma sd 23.0 vs 11.4 and 5th percentile 145 vs 176; lower arcs (x600–840, y440–530) sd 18.4 vs 11.5. Mid-frequency (3–12 px) energy is 8.4–10.1 vs 4.0–5.2. Large-scale structure is weaker than the reference where it matters (band left low-frequency 11.4 vs 14.6; eye outer ring 22.4 vs 26.5). The same pattern shows on the q02 band and diagonal bar (white cloud blobs vs clean flat faces in loop_F030) and on the p06 hold band (x520–960, y410–530: large smeared white blobs, like an upscaled cloud texture).
issues.suggested_fix: Make clear vs frosted a gentle variation in clarity, not a mask. (a) Raise the minimum blur of everything seen through the ice (floor lodFar at ~2.5–3 mips at 1440 px; raise uR11E.w, the panorama blur floor), so sky clouds and the frame copy never read as shapes through a ring. (b) Compress the Noise A roughness ramp (e.g. 0.45–0.9 instead of 0.233–1.0) and reduce the frosted-diffuse swing (uR11D.z), so patches differ by about 8 luma levels, not about 30. (c) Stretch the frost noise 3–4x along the ring tangent (sample Noise A in (s/4, r, z) of the ring frame), so variation becomes long streaks. (d) Let the large-scale structure come from the trace: darker bands where rays cross the far walls or totally reflect, following the ring. Targets on q00: lower-arc luma sd ~12 (now 18.4), mid-frequency energy ~5 (now 8.4).

issues.title: Dotted iso-line contours, parallel contour stripes and pixel sparkle on the ice (likely to crawl in motion)
issues.evidence: zoom_ice_material/p05_eng_toparc_4x.png (p05_expand.png x≈700–880, y≈50–170): closed, dotted bright outlines trace the dark-blue patches on the ring A arc end, like topographic contours or an oil-slick marble. zoom_ice_material/q03_outerR_6x.png (q03_eye.png x≈800–830, y≈260–350): thin parallel light and dark stripes run along the ring, and patches have blocky stair-stepped edges with round white holes. zoom_ice_material/q00_edge_bot_6x.png (q00_rest.png x≈640–760, y≈480–530): salt-and-pepper pixels along ring A's lower arc. Pixel Laplacian on the ice is 2.5–3.4x the reference (q00 lower arcs 12.5 vs 3.7, eye outer ring 14.1 vs 5.5; finest-scale sd 5.1 vs 1.6). The sky baseline differs by only 1.6 vs 0.43, so the excess is in the ice shading, not the codec.
issues.suggested_fix: Band-limit everything that switches inside a pixel. Widen the Noise A ramp filter (fwA ×1.5 → ~×4, +0.02 floor). Widen the critical-angle ramp (uR11N.x / uR11J.y ×2). Fade bump octaves out at a ~1 px footprint instead of 0.3–0.6. Clamp the trace normal to octaves above ~3 px. If it is still visible, supersample only the ice's transmitted term (4-tap rotated grid) or reuse the waterline temporal-AA history on ice pixels. Target ice Laplacian ≤1.5x the reference (now ~3x).

issues.title: Eye pose: inner band (ring D) in front of the orb is a flat, featureless mint ribbon
issues.evidence: zoom_ice_material/q03_band_orb_4x.png. q03_eye.png box x680–770, y382–402: mean RGB 211/230/234 (blue minus green 4, i.e. mint), luma sd 1.9, so it is completely flat. loop_F045 same box: 209/226/240 (blue minus green 14, periwinkle), sd 17.3, with a dark vertical fissure at x≈722–728, darker steel lines along the band's top and bottom edges, a visible top face, and orb plasma wisps visible around the band. The engine shows a smooth pale-aqua strip with a wavy top edge. q01_loop15 inner band (x660–780, y372–406): G 218.5 vs 209.5 (cyan cast), sd 11.5 vs 16.7. The darker refracted edge lines are missing.
issues.suggested_fix: Don't let the clamped orb mean radiance flood the band uniformly. Multiply the orb-through-ice term by the band's facet, frost and crack transmission variation, and keep the sharp orb sample partly visible (lower the lobe width for near-straight paths). Shift light passing from the orb through the ice from mint to periwinkle (G −4, B +6 at equal luma; check the uR11Tint and uFrostTint products on this path). Draw the band's top and bottom face boundaries as darker steel-blue lines (L ~175, blue minus green ~35).

issues.title: Hold close-up lacks the reference's internal refraction drama (far-wall dark line, white refracted orb strip, facet glints) and the band is too dark and saturated
issues.evidence: zoom_ice_material/p06_eng_band_2x.png vs p06_ref_band_2x.png. ref_F420's band shows a dark horizontal far-wall line (y≈395), a clipped-white strip of refracted orb light in its lower centre (x≈640–800, y≈405–440) and a bright facet glint at the top (x≈690–760, y≈290–310). The engine band (p06_sustain.png x520–960, y410–530) is a soft, structureless field. Measured: lower band strip sd 11.2 vs 25.2, 95th percentile 225 vs 255, 5th percentile 192 vs 175. Band face mean luma 200.5 vs 219.6 (~19 levels darker) and saturation 0.186 vs 0.144 (bluer). In p05 the arcs read as wet, swirly glass or chrome rather than frosted ice (p05_pair_1p5x.png).
issues.suggested_fix: Let direct orb-through paths (exit towards the orb after one internal wall) stay sharp and bright: lower their lobe roughness and raise the indirect clamp (uR11M.x) for them, so a white strip of refracted orb light appears in the band's lower half. Render the far-wall total-internal-reflection line as a crisp dark feature (~175 L) at hold distance. Add a tight GGX glint (alpha ~0.03–0.05) per flat facet plateau for the sun and orb. Lift the hold band face by ~+15–19 L and desaturate to ~0.15, to match F420's frosted brightness.

issues.title: Silhouette and cross-section read rounded, pillowy and melted instead of chiselled with flat facets and squared ends
issues.evidence: zoom_ice_material/q02_bandends_4x.png: engine band ends (q02_loop30.png x≈530–560 and x≈880–930, y≈320–430) are rounded barrel or pill caps, and the TIR bar is a soft curved blotch (x≈580–592). loop_F030 has squared ends with a straight vertical dark TIR line (x≈572–582 and x≈865), a flat top face and angular corners. The diagonal bar's top end is a rounded blob in the engine and a squared, chiselled block in loop_F030. zoom_ice_material/p06_leftseg_pair_3x.png: the engine's open ring-D segment end (p06_sustain.png x≈350–480, y≈310–490) is a rounded puffy lobe, while ref_F420's ring end (x≈560–640, y≈235–300) is a flat octagonal cut face with crisp facet edges. The q00 band's top edge is a soft wave in the engine and a straight edge with small notches in F000.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the section and displacement read chiselled. Use sharper octagon corners (reduce the uR11F.z corner rounding). Use flat plateau facets with narrower steps (smaller uR11Ramp), so cells meet in crisp creases. Make shading normals piecewise-constant per cell (uR11H.x = 1 with a higher slope gain), so each facet takes its own value. Cut piece ends as planar caps with a small chamfer, not displaced rounded lobes, and calm the low-frequency wobble on the band's top and bottom edges. If the mesh's lens section limits this, re-export the ring pieces from the artist's EXPORT.blend in Blender 5.2 with SubD-L1 and the Voronoi plateau displacement applied, so the outline matches the Cycles render.

issues.title: Uniform mint-white rim traces every silhouette; the reference has a neutral rim with a steel-blue grazing line inside it
issues.evidence: Profiles across the eye pose's outer-ring right edge. q03_eye.png rows y=300 and y=340, x≈877–886: rim L 211–227 with blue minus green 5–14 (mint), against sky at 21–22. A second inner mint line sits at x≈870–872 (L 219–222, blue minus green 9–10). loop_F045 same rows: rim L 209–223 with blue minus green 19–24 (neutral blue-white), and a darker steel-blue line just inside the edge (y=300, x≈865–869: L 173–179, blue minus green 34–37). At 6x (q03_outerR_6x.png, q00_edge_TR_6x.png) the engine rim is a constant-width pale outline around the whole ring, a CG outline tell.
issues.suggested_fix: Tint the grazing Fresnel and the orb glint on inner rims with the ice tint (periwinkle) instead of the orb's cyan-white. Modulate the rim by facet orientation so it breaks up. Add the steel-blue grazing darkening 3–5 px inside the silhouette, as in F045.

issues.title: No legible cracks or scrape streaks: the fine frost detail has the wrong character
issues.evidence: The reference has real fracture detail: a dark crack across the loop_F030 band centre (x≈705–735, y≈358–385); a vertical fissure through ring D in loop_F045 (x≈722–728, y≈382–410); fine horizontal scrape streaks over the F000 band face (x600–870, y350–415); chipped grain in F420. In every pose the engine's fine content is soft cloud mottling plus pixel noise, with no crack anywhere (see the q00_band_2x.png, q02_center_2x.png and q03_band_orb_4x.png zooms).
issues.suggested_fix: Add 1–3 sparse, larger crack sheets per ring: thin planar fractures in the volume that refract dark on one side and bright on the other (the uCrack path exists; use few, large planes). Add a band-limited fine-streak normal stretched along the ring tangent at 2–6 px scale, in place of the isotropic fine bump.

issues.title: TIR bars at the band ends are too weak and soft at rest
issues.evidence: Row y=385. Left end: q00_rest.png reaches min L 161 (blue minus green 33) at x≈568–571 after a soft 15 px ramp from x≈555. ref_F000 has a crisp ~5 px dark steel line at x≈583–590 reaching L 123 (blue minus green 40). Right end: engine 128–141 at x≈880–885 vs F000 98–105 at x≈878–880. These bars are what make F000's band read as a thick flat slab with frosted end blocks.
issues.suggested_fix: Narrow and deepen the TIR bar: tent half-width ~3 cm → ~1.5 cm, minimum L ~120–130 with blue minus green ~40, keep the wobble. Remove the soft ramp leading into it.

issues.title: Slight cyan cast in the ice overall (reference leans periwinkle or lavender)
issues.evidence: At equal luminance the engine's blue channel is 3–7 levels lower: q00 band left B 226.6 vs 230.0, band right 218.1 vs 225.2. Blue minus red is 42/48 vs 47/53. The q01 inner band has G 218.5 vs 209.5. The mint inner band and mint rims above are the extreme cases of the same bias.
issues.suggested_fix: Shift the ice output ~3–5 levels towards blue or lavender (B +4, G −2 at equal luminance), via uR11Tint or a final ice-only grade, after fixing the mint orb path.

judges.verdict:
Holistic jury score: 7.6. At rest the scene is close to the Cycles reference. The camera, horizon, palette, mountain and iceberg silhouettes, floe rows, rocks and mirror lake all line up, and region colours differ by about 10 RGB or less. The cursor-orbit views hold up as a true 3D world, with clean parallax, no doubled mountains and no seams. The UI is a near-pixel match to the Figma frame. A demanding art director would still flag it side by side, and the hold state shows CG tells. Five things stand between this and a 10/10, in order:
(1) The ice looks like frosted resin with a large, blotchy cloud print, not clear, deep ice that bends the light.
(2) There is no camera-lens feel. The background is rendered in focus and the waterline mist is thin, so the reference's shallow depth of field and haze are missing, most of all during the hold.
(3) The orb is a flat, blown-out white disc with an even lavender rim. In the reference it is a glass sphere that shows a refracted world inside, around a glowing core, with a cyan/violet rim.
(4) When the rings open, the ends are lumpy, rounded 'bone' caps, and the sustain shape is hard to read ('Saturn with ear-muffs', or a jaw in sw_hold_B). The reference shows crisp, saw-cut slabs.
(5) The bottom of the frame during the dolly-in shows a giant smooth ripple arc with blocky crests, and in the pop an untextured grey rock sliver in the bottom-left corner. This is the 'weird at the bottom' the client ruled out.
Smaller issues: the mountain, floe and iceberg bakes (weak rock ribs, no floe glow), granular sparkle in the mid-field water, refraction contour fringes and stair-steps, and the Sound icon (flat line where Figma has a wave). All of these can be fixed with shaders or re-bakes; none needs a render blend.
Not verified: in the sweep hold frames the headline is still fully drawn over the opened sculpture. Confirm the ink dissolve really plays during a live hold.
Zoom evidence is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-muhamadrifaldi-Documents-GitHub-retrux-hero-rnd/a0f5735b-9a7f-477e-9b57-6de40ca5644b/scratchpad/p3/r11_1/zoom_awwwards_jury/
strengths: Rest composition is near 1:1 with the reference (cmp_q00_rest): camera height, horizon line, mountain and iceberg silhouettes, floe rows, foreground rocks and ripple centre all sit in the same place; region_stats_q00 shows engine vs reference within about 10 RGB in almost every region.
Palette and grade match the reference mood: sky gradient, soft volumetric-looking clouds, blue-white snow and the cobalt shard accent.

The real 3D environment survives the cursor orbit: ptr_left and ptr_bottom_right (az ±4.9°) show believable parallax of mountains, iceberg and floes, with no doubled mountains, no seams and no plate smearing (zoom ptr_horizons.png); the orb push-in (ptr_orb) is clean.
The planar mirror lake convinces: real reflections of floes and iceberg, concentric ripples centred under the sculpture, and a clean anti-aliased waterline at rest.

The idle tumble matches the Default Loop: q01 (vertical ring with the cyan inner band), q02 (crossed tubes) and q03 (the eye) read the same as loop F015/F030/F045, including the cyan tint of the inner band.
The cobalt faceted shards, with crisp specular edges, match the reference's colour, scale and look.
The UI overlay is a near-pixel match to the Figma frame: R logo, nav, headline font, leading and position, sub-copy, and the placement of Scroll to Explore and Sound (crop_ui_rest_copy.jpg).

The interaction has real wow moments: the p05 spiral vortex, the sw_pop_T tunnel-eye and the sw_rel_BL release spiral are striking, and the dolly plus fog lift feel cinematic; 60 fps on an Iris 640 at the low tier is a strong developer-award point.

issues.title: Ice ring material reads as frosted resin with a blotchy cloud print, not clear refracting ice
issues.evidence: zoom_awwwards_jury/band_q00_2x.png (q00_rest.png vs ref_F000.png, crop x510-930 y290-470): the engine band (full-frame x~635-790, y~350-415) shows large soft white and blue camouflage patches, like a printed cloud texture, with no internal structure. The reference band is a flat slab of clear ice with fine frost grain, and dark inner-edge lines at x~585 and x~875 (y~350-420) where the far wall of the band shows through; the orb's cyan glow reads through its lower half. zoom_awwwards_jury/ringedge_q03_3x.png (q03_eye vs loop_F045, x770-920 y200-440): the engine shows isotropic blotches with thin bright contour fringes (x~787-813, y~210-233) and a doubled rim line along the outer silhouette (x~870-880, y~250-367). The reference shows soft cobalt streaks running ALONG each ring's axis (a refracting cylinder squeezes the background into long streaks), with lighter edges and a darker core. Also visible in crop_q00_rest_hero.jpg, crop_q03_eye_hero.jpg and crop_p06_sustain_hero.jpg (the band centre is a cloud-print camo pattern).
issues.suggested_fix: (a) Cut the large-scale normal perturbation that drives the refraction offset by about 60-70%, and add a fine micro-frost/crack detail normal (tiled 4-8x denser, low amplitude) so the surface reads as clear ice with fine grain. (b) Make the refraction anisotropic: build the offset in tube space, mostly across each ring's minor axis, so the background compresses into long dark and light streaks along the rings. (c) Add thickness-driven Beer-Lambert absorption (cool cobalt, darker toward the tube core and at grazing back faces). Add a back-face refraction pre-pass so the band's far wall shows as dark inner-edge lines. (d) Raise transmission and lower the milky scatter so the orb glow reads through the band as clean cyan. (e) Optionally bake per-ring thickness and internal-streak masks in Blender/Cycles from the reconstruction. (f) Sample the scene-colour buffer with a roughness-driven mip or small blur to remove contour fringes and the doubled rim.

issues.title: No photographic lens: background in focus and waterline mist too thin (strongest in the hold)
issues.evidence: zoom_awwwards_jury/iceberg_q00_2x.png (q00 x900-1260 y310-460): the engine iceberg is crisp, with fine texture right down to the waterline. In the reference it is clearly defocused, and a white-blue mist veil swallows its lower third (full-frame y~395-460). zoom_awwwards_jury/leftmtn_p06.png (p06 x0-520 y290-590 vs F420 x0-520 y340-640): during the hold the reference mountain is fully defocused and mist covers about 40% of its height. The engine's ridges stay razor sharp under a thin, flat mist band. crop_q00_rest_right.jpg and crop_q00_rest_mountains.jpg show the same at rest. The engine reads as infinite-focus CG; the reference reads as a lens.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a half-resolution, depth-based gather depth of field: blur size from linear depth, focused at the orb distance, with about 3-4 px blur on the iceberg and mountains at rest (1440 px wide) and about 2 px on the near water. Rack the focus during the hold, so camExpand drives the background blur up to about 8-10 px as in F402/F420; the low tier can use a 2-mip blend. Thicken the waterline mist into a height-fog band (0 to about 15% of iceberg height) at about 2x the current density at the iceberg and mountain bases, and let fogHold raise the mist to cover about 40% of the left mountains.

issues.title: Orb is a flat, blown-out white disc with an even lavender rim; it needs a refracting crystal sphere with a glowing core
issues.evidence: zoom_awwwards_jury/orb_q03_3x.png (q03 x605-845 y270-450): the engine orb (x~655-792, y~303-437) is a uniform white disc with an even lavender rim. The reference sphere shows a refracted grey 'nucleus' inside (x~692-748, y~353-380), with a cyan rim on the left and violet on the right. zoom_awwwards_jury/orb_p05_2x.png (p05 x570-870 y250-510 vs F402 x570-870 y300-560): the engine shows a clipped white disc with a blue outline ring. F402 shows a glass ball with an inverted landscape refracted inside, a white glowing core and an iridescent edge. During the hold the orb is the focal point, so the flat look is most exposed there (sw_hold_L, p05, p06).
issues.suggested_fix: Turn the orb into a refractive glass shell (IOR about 1.45) that samples the environment or scene buffer with the inversion a real sphere gives, wrapped around a smaller emissive core (about 60% of the radius). Use per-channel IOR offsets (about R 1.44 / G 1.46 / B 1.49) or a thin-film term for a cyan/violet rim instead of the even lavender fresnel. Keep the core below clipping (about 0.85-0.9 before bloom) so its structure survives, and add a slow internal swirl or caustic drift.

issues.title: Opened rings: lumpy, rounded 'bone' end caps and a sustain shape that is hard to read
issues.evidence: crop_p06_sustain_hero.jpg, left half: the side pieces at crop x~50-190 and x~640-790 are rounded, knobby 'ear' caps. The reference segments (right half, for example the top arc ending at crop x~1340-1360, y~90-180) have crisp flat-cut faces and rectangular cross-sections. sw_hold_TR.png: the tube ends at x~380-450, y~225-330 and x~930-1070, y~425-560 look like chew-toy or bone knobs. sw_hold_B.png: the sustain shape reads as a jaw or mouth with two handles (band y~240-385, bowl y~385-550, knobs at x~355-490 and x~990-1085) instead of an obviously opened sculpture. cmp_p04_expand_pop.jpg: the F358 slabs have saw-cut ends that catch light.
issues.suggested_fix: Give each opened ring segment flat, saw-cut end faces (planar caps with a small sharp bevel and their own refraction and specular glint, with no displacement on the cap). Push the opening offsets further (outer arc gap at least about 0.6x the tube width), and stage the outer arcs as a clean radial bloom around the core in the camera plane (N/E/S/W, as in F453/F460) so the opened state reads at a glance. Keep the client's continuous rotation, but avoid moments where the knobs sit at the band's ends. Optionally deepen the sustain dolly so the band fills about 40% of the frame width, as in F420.

issues.title: Bottom of frame during the dolly: giant smooth ripple arc with blocky crests, plus an untextured rock sliver
issues.evidence: zoom_awwwards_jury/bottom_p05.png and bottom_p06.png: the engine shows one frame-wide smooth arc with flat, untextured bands (p05 y~706-766; p06 y~716-726 edge, x~130-1440). It reads like the rim of a plate or puddle. F402/F420 show choppy, defocused near water there. zoom_awwwards_jury/br_p05_2x.png (p05 x960-1440 y656-766): the ripple crest breaks into blocky, pixelated stair-step patches (x~1150-1410, y~706-751), which looks like a magnified low-resolution normal/height map. zoom_awwwards_jury/bl_sliver_p04_6x.png and bl_p04_vs_ref.png: a featureless flat grey-blue shape intrudes at x0-40, y700-766 in p04 and sw_pop_L. F358 has only water there. The same smooth bands appear in bottom_holds.png (sw_hold_L/TR). The client explicitly asked for nothing weird at the bottom.
issues.suggested_fix: Fade the ripple-ring amplitude with distance from the ripple centre and at grazing view angles near the lens, so the outermost ring never forms a frame-wide arc. Add near-field high-frequency wave normals (choppier within a few metres of the camera) with mipmapped, anisotropic sampling to remove the blocky crest texels, and let the foreground depth of field soften it. For the sliver, cull or move that foreground rock for the hold and pop cameras, or fix its bake or material assignment so it is not drawn flat grey.

issues.title: Environment bakes: mountains read as smooth clay, floes as grey slabs, iceberg slightly washed out
issues.evidence: zoom_awwwards_jury/mountain_q00.png (q00 x60-580 y180-440): the engine's main peak (x~160-530) is smooth snow with few dark rock ribs. The reference shows strong dark rock striations along the ridges. zoom_awwwards_jury/floes_q00.png (q00 x880-1440 y440-590): the engine floe faces are mid-grey, like concrete, with short, dim reflections (y~460-500). The reference floes glow cyan-white with bright vertical reflection columns. region_stats: far floes engine 162,182,204 vs ref 172,189,208; iceberg engine 147,167,191 vs ref 137,155,183 (the engine iceberg is lighter and less cobalt).
issues.suggested_fix: Re-bake the main mountain at higher texel density with the exposed-rock layer (dark ribs along ridges) from the artist's material, and add a tiling detail normal. Give the floe faces a cyan-white translucency/SSS lift, and lengthen and brighten their mirror reflection columns. Deepen the iceberg face toward cobalt, about -10 RGB.

issues.title: Mid-field water has granular glitter noise and soft, low-contrast ripple bands
issues.evidence: crop_q00_rest_water.jpg: the engine water (top) carries even, fine, sparkly noise across the whole mid-field, with broad, soft ripple bands. The reference (bottom) is a smoother mirror with crisper, darker concentric ripple troughs and a stronger cyan-white glint near the bottom centre. region_stats: water near engine 167,180,200 vs ref 177,189,209.
issues.suggested_fix: Reduce the high-frequency sparkle normal by about 50% in the mid-field. Sharpen the ripple ring profile (narrower crests, darker troughs). Boost and cool the near glint toward the reference's cyan-white highlight.

issues.title: Refraction aliasing: contour fringes, stair-stepped streaks and pixel speckle that will crawl in motion
issues.evidence: zoom_awwwards_jury/ringfringe_q03_6x.png (q03 x775-885 y205-315): thin bright cyan contour lines trace the blotch edges, and the silhouette shows stair-steps. zoom_awwwards_jury/refr_stair_p05_6x.png (p05 x810-910 y330-430): stair-stepped refraction streaks and single-pixel speckles inside the ring near the orb. These would shimmer during the tumble and the hold.
issues.suggested_fix: Run the refractive pass through the TAA, or supersample it 2x. Sample the refraction source with a roughness-based mip and clamp offsets near silhouettes so the bright edges of other objects are not picked up as fringes.

issues.title: UI: Sound indicator shows a flat line where the Figma frame shows a wave glyph
issues.evidence: crop_ui_rest_sound.jpg: the engine shows a straight line before 'Sound'; the Figma frame shows a small sine-wave glyph. Every other UI element matches.
issues.suggested_fix: Use the Figma wave glyph (gently animated while sound plays). If the flat line is meant as the muted state, confirm that with the designer.

judges.verdict: The palette, brightness, scale and density are right. The orb core is about as bright as the reference's, its size inside the rings matches, the shard hue is exact and over the idle poses the shard count and area are equal. Up close, though, both elements read as CG. The orb is a flat disc of clipped white with a thick lavender-blue fresnel rim and a dark outline. judges.verdict: The environment is a faithful, premium rebuild of the reference. Layout, silhouettes, sky, clouds and overall colour all match. The real 3D geometry holds up under every cursor orbit (no doubled mountains) and through the hold dolly (no plate stretching or tearing). Side by side, though, a demanding art director would still flag several CG tells: (1) The main mountain reads as smooth clay. Its rock gullies are missing and a straight horizontal haze stripe crosses its face. (2) The iceberg and right shoreline lack the milky mist at the waterline that every reference frame shows, so the iceberg base is about 50 RGB levels too dark and too crisp. (3) The ripple ring looks like painted shadow bands rather than physical waves. (4) In the hold, the near ripple ring turns into a smooth curved 'glass plate' across the bottom of the frame, exactly the 'weird bottom' the client warned about, and the fog over the mountain bases is a thin flat gradient instead of F420's billowing bank. (5) The far lake has regular striped micro-ripple and weak reflection pillars instead of a glassy mirror. (6) The dark left ridge is too light and faceted, and when the cursor orbits right it shows black slits. Everything here can be fixed with shader work, mist cards or Blender re-bakes; none of it needs render blending.
